consensus_summary: Consensus responses identify 'rich' primarily as worldly/material self-sufficiency and spiritual danger or hindrance (misplaced trust, often masking poverty as in Laodicea), with a common dual alternative of true spiritual wealth/richness toward God in faith/grace; secondary strands include OT blessing, stewardship, or oppression.
book_summary: The self-sufficient who “have need of nothing”—full of self and unable to receive (Laodicea’s boast, Smyrna’s opposite); true wealth is being “rich toward God”: faith tried in the fire and the garment of righteousness.
consensus_core_identification: Worldly richness as self-sufficiency/spiritual peril (ironic poverty) versus true spiritual richness toward God.
book_core_identification: Self-sufficient (need nothing, full of self, unable to receive; Laodicea vs. Smyrna) versus true wealth as rich toward God (tried faith, righteousness garment).
boundary_disagreement: None material; both center on Laodicean self-sufficiency and inverted spiritual richness via the same key texts.
rationale: Minimum cores are equivalent: both take the dominant referent as the self-sufficient (Laodicea-style boast of needing nothing, spiritual peril/poverty) and the positive inversion as richness toward God (faith/spiritual goods). Shared proof texts (Rev 3:17–18, Rev 2:9, Luke 12:21) confirm identity of referent; extra consensus alternatives (blessing, oppression) are non-primary and do not alter the core match; wording differences are immaterial.
strongest_objection: Some responses treat the term as having no single settled sense and list broader alternatives (OT blessing, class oppression) that the entry does not address, which could be read as selective emphasis rather than full equivalence.
